explanation: The line comes from Yeats's poem 'The Second Coming', written in 1919: 'Things fall apart; the centre cannot hold.' Achebe's 1958 novel follows an Igbo leader as colonial rule arrives.

claims.text: The title Things Fall Apart is taken from a line in W. B. Yeats's poem The Second Coming.
The title is not taken from a poem by T. S. Eliot, Wole Soyinka or Rudyard Kipling.
Yeats's poem The Second Coming contains the line 'Things fall apart; the centre cannot hold'.
Yeats wrote The Second Coming in 1919.
Things Fall Apart was published in 1958 and follows Okonkwo, an Igbo leader, as British colonial rule arrives.
